0.headline: Credent Connect N Care IPO sees over 142 times subscription on final day, GMP remains strong since launch
0.heading: Credent Connect N Care IPO sees over 142 times subscription on final day, GMP remains strong since launch
0.intro: Credent Connect N Care IPO | The company entered the capital markets last week to raise up to Rs 93.9 crore through its maiden public issue at the upper end of the price band of Rs 179-189 per share.
0.body:
Ashish Kacholia- and Sunil Singhania-backed healthcare logistics services provider Credent Connect N Care's initial public offering continued to attract a robust response from investors across categories, with the issue subscribed 142.38 times on August 17, the final day of bidding.

The company entered the capital markets last week to raise up to Rs 93.9 crore through its maiden public issue at the upper end of the price band of Rs 179-189 per share. The IPO comprised an entirely fresh issuance of 49.68 lakh shares.

Investors placed bids for 50.74 crore equity shares over the three-day bidding period, against the offer size of 35.64 lakh shares, through 2.3 lakh applications. The bids were worth Rs 9,590 crore at the higher end of the price range, which is 27 times higher than the company's market capitalisation.

Non-institutional investors led the subscription numbers, bidding 217.3 times their allotted quota, while the portion reserved for retail investors was subscribed 138.85 times and the portion allocated to qualified institutional buyers was subscribed 130.39 times.

Credent Connect N Care is expected to finalise the IPO share allotment by August 18, and its equity shares will be available for trading on the NSE Emerge platform on August 20.

Credent Connect shares continued to trade at a 29 percent premium in the grey market, market observers said. The grey market is an unofficial market for trading in IPO shares until their listing on the stock exchanges.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

The Delhi-headquartered company provides business-to-business healthcare logistics services, including the transportation of diagnostic samples from collection points to laboratories and between healthcare facilities. It also provides services to in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) companies for the movement of reagents from their C&amp;F locations to laboratories.

As of June 2026, the company operated a fleet of 97 commercial vehicles used for sample transportation and related logistics operations, along with two warehouses and four branch offices across India, including in Mumbai, Pune, Chennai and Varanasi.

Credent Connect N Care will utilise Rs 29.8 crore of the proceeds from the net offer size for working capital requirements and capital expenditure on machinery for its subsidiary, Credent Healthcare. Further, Rs 37 crore will be used for its working capital requirements, Rs 6 crore for debt repayment, and the remaining funds for general corporate purposes.

Ace investor Ashish Kacholia owned a 2.02 percent stake in Credent Connect, while Sunil Singhania's Abakkus Asset Manager, through its Abakkus Venture Opportunities Fund, held a 2.26 percent stake in the company.

Hem Securities is acting as the merchant banker for the Credent Connect N Care IPO.

1.headline: Tempsens Instruments IPO GMP nears 44% ahead of subscription; check lot size, timeline and other key details here
1.heading: Tempsens Instruments IPO GMP nears 44% ahead of subscription; check lot size, timeline and other key details here
1.intro: Tempsens Instruments (India) is seeing strong grey-market interest ahead of the opening of its initial public offering (IPO) on August 20, with the unofficial premium currently indicating a potential listing gain of more than 43 percent over the upper end of its price band.
1.body:
Tempsens Instruments (India) is seeing strong grey-market interest ahead of the opening of its initial public offering (IPO) on August 20, with the unofficial premium currently indicating a potential listing gain of more than 43 percent over the upper end of its price band.

According to IPO-tracking platform InvestorGain, Tempsens Instruments IPO is commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of Rs 130 over the upper price band of Rs 300. This implies a premium of about 43.33 percent and points to an indicative listing price of around Rs 430 if the grey-market trend holds.

Investors must note that the grey market premiums are unofficial and based on market speculation. They do not guarantee listing gains or reflect the company's fundamentals.

Read Also: Class 5 dropout, now owns Rs 11,000 crore Lalithaa Jewellery: How Kiran Kumar turned his mother's 4 gold bangles into a business empire

The Rajasthan-based company has fixed the price band for its Rs 650-crore IPO at Rs 285 to Rs 300 per share. At the upper end of the price band, Tempsens Instruments is looking at a market capitalisation of around Rs 2,515 crore. The IPO will open for subscription on August 20 and close on August 24, with the anchor investor bidding scheduled for August 19.

The issue comprises a fresh share sale of Rs 95 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 1.85 crore equity shares worth Rs 555 crore. The company will not receive proceeds from the shares sold by existing shareholders under the OFS.

The company has reserved shares worth Rs 1.5 crore for its employees. Of the net issue, excluding the employee portion, 50 percent has been reserved for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), 35 percent for retail investors and 15 percent for non-institutional investors (NIIs).

The minimum bid size is 50 shares. At the upper price band of Rs 300, retail investors will need a minimum investment of Rs 15,000. The maximum retail application is 650 shares, requiring Rs 1.95 lakh.

The IPO allotment is expected to be finalised on August 25, while the company's shares are likely to be listed on the stock exchanges on August 28.

Tempsens Instruments is the sixth mainboard IPO to hit the primary market this week, after Lalithaa Jewellery Mart, Horizon Industrial Parks, Sunshine Pictures, Shankesh Jewellers and Gaja Capital.

Tempsens Instruments plans to deploy Rs 18.1 crore from the net fresh issue towards capital expenditure for its electrical heating solutions and specialised cable solutions businesses.

Another Rs 55 crore is earmarked for debt repayment, with the balance proposed to be used for general corporate purposes.

Check IPO News Here

Tempsens Instruments reported a profit of Rs 67.3 crore for the financial year ended March 2026, compared with Rs 60.6 crore in the previous year, marking growth of 11.2 percent.

Revenue increased 17.5 percent year-on-year to Rs 444.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 378.5 crore in FY25.

ICICI Securities and JM Financial are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

About Tempsens Instruments

The company describes itself as a manufacturer of contact and non-contact temperature sensors and operates across three key business verticals, including temperature sensing solutions, electrical heating solutions and specialised cables. Tempsens Instruments has a reported 10.5 percent market share in the temperature sensor segment and 21.3 percent in the non-contact temperature sensor market. It operates 15 manufacturing facilities globally through the company, subsidiaries and joint ventures, including 10 facilities in Udaipur and five overseas.

2.headline: Horizon Industrial Parks IPO booked 14% on Day 1, latest GMP here
2.heading: Horizon Industrial Parks IPO booked 14% on Day 1, latest GMP here
2.intro: Blackstone-backed Horizon Industrial Parks' initial public offering (IPO) received a muted response on the opening day of bidding, with the issue subscribed 14 percent by 5:00 pm on August 17, according to data from the NSE.
2.body:
Blackstone-backed Horizon Industrial Parks' initial public offering (IPO) received a muted response on the opening day of bidding, with the issue subscribed 14 percent by 5:00 pm on August 17, according to data from the NSE.

The Rs 2,600-crore IPO received bids for 3,52,85,000 shares against 25,13,56,273 shares on offer. Retail investors led the demand, subscribing to 19 percent of the portion reserved for them, while the Non-Institutional Investor (NII) category was subscribed 3 percent.

The public issue will remain open until August 19. The IPO comprises entirely a fresh issue of equity shares, with the company having fixed the price band at Rs 57-60 per share.

Read Also: Lalithaa Jewellery IPO subscribed 11% so far on opening day; GMP signals 15% listing premium

In the grey market, Horizon Industrial Parks shares are commanding a premium of Rs 3.5 over the upper end of the IPO price band, according to Investorgain and IPO Watch.

At the upper price band of Rs 60, the current grey market premium (GMP) of Rs 3.5 implies an estimated listing price of Rs 63.5. This translates into a potential listing gain of nearly 6 percent, if the GMP holds until listing.

Investors must note that the GMP is an unofficial indicator and does not guarantee the actual listing price.

Ahead of the public issue, Horizon Industrial Parks raised around Rs 1,167.8 crore from 54 anchor investors. The anchor book included global and institutional names such as Morgan Stanley, Carmignac, Millennium Management, Societe Generale, Citigroup Global and Viridian Asset Management.

The company allotted 19.46 crore equity shares to anchor investors at the upper end of the Rs 57-60 price band on August 14.

Domestic mutual funds accounted for 3.88 crore shares of the anchor allocation. These shares were allotted to six fund houses, including WhiteOak Capital, Sundaram Mutual Fund, 360 ONE, PGIM India, JM Financial and Edelweiss, through 27 schemes.

SBI Life Insurance and Edelweiss Life Insurance were allotted another 1.24 crore shares worth around Rs 75 crore.

Horizon Industrial Parks plans to use Rs 2,250 crore of the net IPO proceeds to repay debt, while the remaining funds will be deployed towards general corporate purposes.

The company had outstanding borrowings of Rs 6,884.3 crore as of March 2026, making debt reduction a key component of its IPO strategy.

Check IPO News Here

Despite a sharp rise in revenue, the company remained loss-making in FY26. Its net loss widened to Rs 203.6 crore from Rs 178.7 crore in FY25. Revenue increased 77.1 percent to Rs 691.4 crore from Rs 390.3 crore during the same period.

It operates 45 assets across 10 cities, including Delhi-NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Pune, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Nagpur.

The company is owned and managed by three Blackstone affiliates, which collectively held an 88.74 percent stake before the IPO.

JM Financial, Axis Capital, IIFL Capital Services, SBI Capital Markets and 360 ONE WAM are the book-running lead managers to the issue.

About Horizon Industrial Parks

Horizon Industrial Parks is an industrial and logistics infrastructure developer and operator with a portfolio spanning major industrial and consumption hubs in India. The company provides Grade A warehouses, industrial facilities and in-city logistics centres, along with services such as cold storage, energy solutions, on-site staff accommodation, racking and material-handling equipment.
